facts.fact: The bear held the narrow place against all comers until first light. Vellan then sent Kamalakshi and a Company runner down asking for the Warden alone and ordered everyone else kept away; that is why no one reached him before Devan.
Two dead are named on Kandan's chalked tile at dawn: Lekha, of the Company, and Sreedhar, a drover of Kalladi (garrison volunteer). Neela's lips move on both names.

Neela had told Devan the number 310 at the ledger (B2 ch16). In ch27 she gives its meaning: she kept counting hoping whoever was on the stair would finish before she reached the end. She was not blindfolded at the lamp; 'they took the lamp and told me to count'.
Per bible dating (Asha's death six years before book 1) the chapter drops explicit year counts for Devan's guarded back and Vellan's burden, writing 'since Asha' / 'ever since'.
